description: Market-access pathway ruleset. Pure data extracted from the upstream app's src/lib/pathway-rules.ts, decoupled from UI per docs/open-source-ruleset-strategy.md: icon → sectionType, colorTheme → pathwayType, ISO 3166 lowercase jurisdictions, dossier category taxonomy. Evaluate with scripts/evaluate.ts.

selection.note: Base pathway is keyed only on (jurisdiction, category), faithful to the source's evaluatePathway. riskClass and hasAI never select the base pathway — they only add warnings/insights. Resolution order: exact (jurisdiction, category) → jurisdiction default → globalDefault.

pathways.stopper: WZW Criteria: Must prove clinical benefit for mild-to-moderate depression with CBT approach.
pathways.roleDescription: Preparation of MiGeL application for digital cognitive behavioral therapy applications.
pathways.expertInsight: NEW PATHWAY: As of July 1, 2026, Switzerland introduces its first dedicated dGA category for cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT) apps treating mild-to-moderate depression. This is Switzerland's first DiGA-like pathway. Apps must be prescribed by physicians with required specialist title and used as adjunct or bridge to psychotherapy.
pathways.adoptionBarrier: Physician prescription required; limited to depression CBT indication initially.

requirements.label: Swiss Market Authorization
requirements.description: Registration with Swissmedic or MRA recognition.

requirements.label: Clinical Efficacy Dossier
requirements.description: Evidence for CBT effectiveness in mild-to-moderate depression.

pathways.stopper: WZW: Must prove Economy (Wirtschaftlichkeit) vs existing methods.
pathways.roleDescription: Application for a new medical service position in the tariff structure.
pathways.expertInsight: TARDOC is replacing TARMED in the ambulatory setting. Ensure applications reference the appropriate tariff structure.

requirements.label: Tariff Proposal
requirements.description: Formal request to tariff partners (FMH, curafutura).

requirements.label: Budget Impact
requirements.description: Cost comparison to standard of care.

pathways.stopper: WZW Criteria: Must prove Analytical Validity & Clinical Utility.
pathways.roleDescription: Application for inclusion in the List of Analyses (Analysenliste).
pathways.expertInsight: For diagnostic labs, the Analysenliste (AL) determines reimbursement. New markers require explicit addition. Must demonstrate WZW (Efficiency, Appropriateness, Economy) and often requires HTA-like evidence of clinical utility.

requirements.label: Analysenliste Application
requirements.description: Formal request for new analysis code.

requirements.label: Clinical Validity Dossier
requirements.description: Evidence of sensitivity, specificity, and clinical impact.

pathways.roleDescription: Preparation of the Mittel- und Gegenständeliste (MiGeL) application.
pathways.expertInsight: MiGeL is primarily for devices used by patients themselves or with non-professional help. Devices used by healthcare professionals in clinical settings may follow different pathways (TARMED, SwissDRG). Trust Principle may apply for physician-led digital services.
pathways.adoptionBarrier: MiGeL focuses on self-administered devices; professional-use devices may need alternative pathways.

requirements.label: WZW Assessment Dossier
requirements.description: Structuring evidence for Efficacy and Appropriateness.

requirements.label: Health Economic Analysis
requirements.description: Budget impact for Swiss basic insurance.

pathways.stopper: Status 1 Funding: Requires proof of 'Novelty' and economic gap.
pathways.roleDescription: Generation of NUB requests for hospital innovation funding.

pathways.stopper: Valuation Committee: Must prove diagnostic accuracy leads to therapeutic benefit (linked evidence).
pathways.roleDescription: Synthesizing 'Linked Evidence' chains for ambulatory reimbursement.
pathways.adoptionBarrier: Proving clinical utility chain from diagnosis to improved outcomes is extremely challenging.

pathways.stopper: High Evidence Bar: RCTs usually required for new methods.
pathways.roleDescription: Full HTA dossier for hardware-based methods (Methodenbewertung).
pathways.adoptionBarrier: Extremely rigorous evidence requirements; most manufacturers pursue hospital NUB pathway instead.

requirements.label: Systematic Review
requirements.description: Full literature review per IQWiG methods.

pathways.stopper: Positive Care Effect (pVE): Medical benefit or structural improvement required.
pathways.roleDescription: Drafting of the Evaluation Concept and Systematic Literature Search.
pathways.expertInsight: DiPA pathway (Pflegeanwendungen) available for nursing/care apps (SGB XI). DiGA Class IIa maximum currently; Class IIb under discussion with DigiG legislation. Provisional listing allows 12-24 months to generate evidence.
pathways.successRate: ~60% achieve permanent listing after provisional phase
pathways.adoptionBarrier: Low prescription rates by physicians (awareness gap); reimbursement rates often insufficient for sustainability.

requirements.label: MDR CE Mark
requirements.description: Class I or IIa certificate (IIb under discussion).

requirements.label: DiGA Evaluation Concept
requirements.description: Study design for provisional trial period.

pathways.stopper: Innovation: Must fill unmet need. PECAN has strict pricing caps and ~75% rejection rate.
pathways.roleDescription: Generation of the Innovation Note and Matrice Demandeur.
pathways.expertInsight: PECAN covers ALL risk classes (I-III). Strict pricing: DTx €780/year max, telemonitoring €50/month. High rejection rate (~75%). Must justify French healthcare system applicability. Interoperability (ANS) is major barrier.
pathways.expertInsightWhenHasAI: CRITICAL: HAS requires 'White Box' AI transparency - training data sources must be disclosed. PECAN covers ALL risk classes (I-III), unlike DiGA. Pricing: DTx max €780/year (€435 first 3 months), telemonitoring €50/month. Must submit for permanent listing (LPPR for DTx, LATM for telemonitoring) within 6-9 months.
pathways.successRate: ~25% - only 2 of 17 initiated applications successful as of 2024
pathways.adoptionBarrier: Very strict evidence requirements for French system applicability; fixed low pricing discourages many manufacturers.

requirements.label: French System Justification
requirements.description: Evidence applicability to French healthcare context.

pathways.stopper: ASA Level: Improvement of Service Attendu (clinical benefit level).
pathways.adoptionBarrier: CEPS price negotiations can significantly delay market access post-HAS approval.

requirements.label: Clinical Dossier (SA)
requirements.description: Evidence of Service Attendu and ASA improvement.

pathways.stopper: Wide Utilization: CPT Category I requires widespread adoption.
pathways.roleDescription: Drafting CPT Code Applications and Value Analysis decks.
pathways.adoptionBarrier: Requires demonstrated utilization; Category III (temporary) code often necessary first step.

pathways.stopper: TCET: Highly selective (~5 devices/year). Must be FDA Breakthrough AND fit existing Medicare benefit category.
pathways.roleDescription: Drafting CPT Code Applications, TCET nominations, and Value Analysis materials.
pathways.expertInsight: CRITICAL TCET LIMITATIONS: Only ~5 devices/year accepted. Requires FDA Breakthrough designation AND must fit existing Medicare benefit category (excludes most digital health). Quarterly review cycles. Pre-market engagement recommended 12+ months before FDA authorization. Most devices should pursue traditional MAC coverage or CPT coding instead.
pathways.successRate: TCET: <5% of nominations accepted | Traditional NCD: ~30-40% approval rate
pathways.adoptionBarrier: TCET highly competitive and restrictive; most digital health excluded from Medicare coverage due to benefit category limitations.

requirements.label: CPT Application
requirements.description: Category I or III code for billing.

requirements.label: TCET Nomination (Selective)
requirements.description: Transitional Coverage - 12+ month pre-market engagement required.

pathways.stopper: Evidence Standards Framework (ESF) Tier C compliance. DTAC mandatory for NHS procurement.
pathways.roleDescription: Preparation for Early Value Assessment and DTAC compliance.
pathways.expertInsight: DTAC is mandatory entry requirement for NHS digital health market. EVA provides conditional recommendations for 3-4 years while generating real-world evidence. IMPORTANT: NICE recommendations are NOT binding - final adoption decisions made by local Integrated Care Systems (ICSs) based on budget impact.
pathways.successRate: 42 of 90 technologies recommended in EVAs conducted (47%)
pathways.adoptionBarrier: NICE recommendations non-binding; local ICS commissioners make final decisions based on competing budget priorities.

requirements.label: DTAC Compliance
requirements.description: Digital Technology Assessment Criteria (5 pillars: clinical safety, data protection, technical security, interoperability, usability).

requirements.label: NICE EVA Submission
requirements.description: Early Value Assessment dossier for conditional recommendation.

requirements.label: Real-World Evidence Plan
requirements.description: 3-4 year data collection strategy during conditional period.

globalDefault.roleDescription: Strategic mapping of regulatory and reimbursement requirements.

warnings.message: France (HAS) requires 'White Box' AI transparency. Training data sources must be disclosed. PECAN has ~75% rejection rate.
PECAN has strict pricing caps (DTx: €780/year max, telemonitoring: €50/month) and high rejection rate (~75%). Evidence must justify French healthcare system applicability.

TCET is highly selective (~5 devices/year) and excludes most digital health apps unless they fit existing Medicare benefit category. Most manufacturers should pursue traditional MAC coverage or CPT coding.
TCET requires both FDA Breakthrough designation AND fit within existing Medicare benefit categories. Quarterly review cycles only.

CRITICAL: NICE EVA recommendations are NOT binding. Final adoption decisions made by local Integrated Care Systems (ICSs) based on budget priorities. Success rate: ~47% of assessed technologies recommended.

DiGA approval doesn't guarantee adoption. Prescription rates remain low due to physician awareness gaps. ~60% achieve permanent listing after provisional phase. DiPA available for nursing/care apps (SGB XI).
NEW: dGA pathway launching July 1, 2026 for CBT apps treating mild-to-moderate depression. Physician prescription required. First DiGA-like pathway in Switzerland.
Reimbursing a 'Method' is distinct from a 'Device'. Widespread clinical adoption is critical for coding success.
DiGA currently limited to Class I-IIa. Class IIb expansion under discussion with DigiG legislation. High-risk devices must pursue G-BA pathway.

insights.ch: Switzerland launching first dGA pathway (July 2026) for CBT depression apps. MiGeL focuses on patient-administered devices; professional-use follows different pathways (TARMED/TARDOC).
insights.de: Germany offers fastest digital health pathway (DiGA) but adoption remains challenge. DiPA available for nursing apps. G-BA method assessment extremely rigorous (3-5 years).
insights.fr: France's PECAN covers all risk classes but has ~75% rejection rate and strict pricing caps. High bar for French system applicability. Interoperability (ANS) is major technical barrier.
insights.us: TCET highly selective (~5/year) and excludes most digital health. Traditional pathways (MAC coverage, CPT coding) more realistic for most manufacturers. Hospital value committees critical.
insights.uk: DTAC mandatory for NHS digital health. EVA offers conditional coverage but NICE recommendations non-binding - local ICS budget decisions determine real market access.
